institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I was interested in the Geology of the Arctic and fieldwork in the Arctic. UNIS through UIT seemed to be one of the best options for this and it definitely lived up to the expectations I had of lots of field work and accompanying safety instructions on how to operate in the field. I was also excited to see the modern field equipment and data acquisition methods advertised at UNIS and I also received training in using drones for data acquisition in hard to traverse terrain.
This all seemed relevant to the direction i wanted to go with my future studies and career.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a very welcoming community both of fellow students and of professors, i had many opportunities to join for fieldwork outside of the expected course work. I also made many friends i still keep contact with and intend to visit.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UiT and UNIS provided a lot of information in advance of my arrival through various infosites and emails, the overall process was very smooth. When i did need more help, the staff was very helpful in providing it (this was mostly with administrative work regarding getting approval to rent rifles).

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Assigned a room and delivered keys.
Signatures to approve rifle renting.
Introduction to the University Center and Town

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Since the town is quite small it was easy to navigate and get familiar with on your own/ with fellow new students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Samskipnadden (the local student housing company) had a very easy application process. This is the only student housing in the town outside of private renting. You are made aware of this when you apply to UNIS.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Samskipnadden is has a very easy application process. Don't confuse it for the UNIS guest house, this is for visiting professors and researchers.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Only one available but it was very cosy. The room and common kitchens were built in a way that makes it easy to be social, which is important especially in the dark season when the sun doesn't rise. I had very nice kitchenmates that all helped keep it clean and wanted to do activities together even if we had different studies (i am geologist, they were engineers).

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The additional application process to UNIS after having applied to UiT was a little tedious but understandably necessary. I did not feel it was any more complicated than it needed to be.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Apply to exchange to UiT through Copenhagen University's exchange program.
Once accepted send in application to UiT through their søknadsweb site and upload documentation and select courses at UNIS.
At the same time apply separately directly to UNIS through their søknadsweb site. They ask for similar documentation.
Once approved by both institutions send the approval to the host institution.
You also need Copenhagen University to pre-approve your courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The E-mails received contained most of the information needed. Otherwise the information on UiT's website was helpful when i needed clarification on how to have my exchange approved. I did email the institution on one occasion when i was unsure and received good help. There was also a phone nr available, but i never used it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was approved for the classes i wanted, it was a relatively smooth process to register.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the emails recieved from the various institutions carefully, they provide all the information needed to register correctly. If in doubt check the institutions website, UiT had a nice step by step guide for applying. Otherwise email or call if you are ever in doubt about your application.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The program was amazing, the first half of the semester was spent learning the theoretical knowledge and field safety in the arctic to set you up for the second half where you are meant to independently plan fieldwork. It felt very rewarding to apply what was learned in this way.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My 2 courses were The Geological Evolution of Svalbard and Arctic Landforms and Processes. Both were 15 ECTs giving a total of 30 ECTs for the semester. The level of the courses was very satisfactory. I felt academically challenged but never overwhelmed. Level was what i would expect of a bachelor's course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Being in the Arctic, the institution took full advantage of this, with lots of fieldwork to experience the Arctic and see the geology at various sites. The in-class projects were also more independent, requiring us to plan fieldwork to sites up to 20km away from town. This gave a lots of opportunities for independent learning and preparing for more independent work. Overall there was a bigger emphasis on applying knowledge in the field than i am used to at UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
(At UNIS)
AG - 214 Geological Evolution of Svalbard
AG - 215 Arctic Landforms and Processes

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The choice is quite limited to these 2 aforementioned courses in the autumn semester if you are a geologist. There is also a geophysics courses at a bachelor level but i did not take these.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I underestimated the equipment required to do fieldwork in the arctic. I ended up spending an extra 3000DKK on good footwear and clothing.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive but still affordable. You could borrow a lot of equipment from the university center, local community initiatives and student organizations so i saved on various kitchen equipment, books, field equipment, skis, etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is an amazing place to go hiking.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Directly with the institution i attended dance classes.
Outside the institution i joined the local football club and got a gym membership.
On my own and fellow students initiatives I went on several skiing, fishing and hiking trips.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was surprised at how fun dance classes were, i had never done it before. Otherwise hiking and fishing were my favorite.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Weekends allow for longer multi-day hikes, there is a student cabin you can book or you can book a cabin through the local hunting and fishing club.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I already spoke Norwegian and English beforehand which helped as those were the main languages spoken. It is a very international town so you end up meeting a lot of other people who are just as foreign as you are. Speaking Norwegian was still an advantage for being included in the more Norwegian activities.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join for hikes and other activities outside of school. Most of your fellow students don't have family, friends or job or other obligations outside of schoolwork, so they are very available to join for activities.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There was nothing i found challenging culturally. It took a little time to get used to seeing firearms so frequently but at no point did it make me feel unsafe, they were handled with care.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone was very open and caring, both locals and fellow exchange students. This was especially nice during the dark period when the sun didn't rise as you were more likely to become depressed, but the many chances to be social and various events led to this not being an issue for me.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Bring proper equipment to go hiking, you will be in the field no matter what study you come with (geology, biology, engineering etc.) and also to hike outside of school.
Give new opportunities a chance, I was invited to join for lots of activities i never tried before and was pleasantly surprised by them. For me it was dance classes that i never tried before and i ended up enjoying it a lot and making lots of friends through it.
Make lots of friends, you will have a lot of extra time due to not having obligations with family, friends and jobs from home and neither will your fellow students so people are extra friendly and have more time to be social.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are lots of local initiatives like "bruktikken" local charity shop where you can get clothes and various stuff for free. Check local billboards and talk to the locals they'll know all the various events going on in town.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I made some friends for life and was academically challenged to do more independent work.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was very physically demanding to go on fieldwork and going for hikes, especially carrying equipment and supplies in the rough terrain. You will be traveling a lot by foot during this exchange. This is at the same time felt very rewarding.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I very much recommend taking an exchange at UNIS through UiT.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
